title: Sort a K-Sorted Array
statement:
You are given an integer array `arr` of length `n` and an integer `k`. The array is **k-sorted**: if you sorted it in ascending order, every element would end up at most `k` positions away from the position it has now. (If equal values exist, you may break ties between them in whatever way satisfies this.)

Return the array sorted in ascending order. A solution that exploits the k-sorted property is expected: sorting from scratch ignores the guarantee that you were given.

It is guaranteed that the input really is k-sorted. `k = 0` means the array is already sorted.

**Follow-up:** Elements arrive one at a time as a stream and you must emit them in sorted order using only `O(k)` memory. Does your approach still work?
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers, the elements of `arr`.
outputFormat: Print the `n` elements in ascending order, separated by single spaces.

examples.explanation: In sorted order 3 belongs at position 2 (moved by 2) and 6 belongs at position 5 (moved by 2). No element moves more than k = 2.
Each element is at most one step from its sorted position, so adjacent pairs are swapped.
k = 0, the array is already sorted.

hints: The smallest of the remaining elements must be among the next k + 1 elements of the array.
Keep a min-heap holding a sliding window of k + 1 elements.
Pop the minimum to the output, then push the next unread element. When the input ends, pop everything that is left.
